Market Gravity Index (MGI) evaluates directional momentum by aggregating line movement, consensus, timing, injury impact, key number crossing, staleness, and dispersion. It uses bounded functions and sigmoidal transformations to produce a normalized score. Stale Line Risk Score (SLRS) assesses temporal validity and source cleanliness, blocking stale lines regardless of movement. GSE Signal Score (GSS) integrates MGI and SLRS into a coherent decision kernel. Dualities emerge: MGI captures market intent while SLRS ensures signal integrity. Failure modes include stale data invalidating all signals, or insufficient consensus leading to low confidence scores. These primitives form a layered architecture where each layer enforces epistemic constraints before passing to next.
